newsitem.title: UK: Britain's Screamin' Lord Sutch mourns mother.
newsitem.headline: Britain's Screamin' Lord Sutch mourns mother.

text.p: Screamin' Lord Sutch, Britain's longest-serving political party leader, said on Tuesday his mother Annie had died at the age of 80.

Sutch, who heads the Official Monster Raving Loony Party, had decided not to stand in Britain's May 1 election in order to care for his mother while she was in hospital after a hip replacement operation.

It was the first general election Sutch had missed since 1964. Campaigning under the slogan "Vote for Insanity, You Know it Makes Sense", he has stood unsuccessfully for parliament 41 times over the past three decades.
He said Annie had fallen again after the hip replacement and had not recovered. She died on April 30.

Sutch, a rock singer who campaigns in leopardskin tailcoat and top hat, brandishing a megaphone, said he would be wearing a slightly toned down version of his traditional dress at his mother's funeral in north London on May 14.
"It's bad news," Sutch told Reuters. "I thought the world of her. By having me as her son, she really created the Monster Raving Loony Party."
Sutch, 56, said that in losing his mother, he had lost more in the election than the Conservatives, who were roundly trounced in Labour's landslide victory.
The Loony party, the most colourful and most durable of Britain's multitude of fringe groups, put up several candidates in the election.
Sutch said he would now be concentrating on his musical career before returning to the political fray.
"I've been numbed for a while," he said. "But I'll be getting back into doings things now, but it will be music rather than politics for the moment."

Before he went into politics, Sutch ran a 1960s rock band called the Savages in which stars such as Noel Redding of the Jimi Hendrix Experience, Keith Moon of The Who and guitar legend Jeff Beck played early in their careers.
But he still has a five pounds ($8) bet on that he will become prime minister -- at odds of 15 million to one.
